description: Massachusetts Performance Standards for Local Public Health: the mandated local responsibilities and the workforce standards, as listed in DPH's Excel workbook (Office of Local and Regional Health, published 2023-10-11).
not_included: Only the four mandate sheets and the Workforce Standards sheet are read. The workbook's 'Frequently Used' sheet (discretionary board of health powers, such as appointing agents), 'Resources', and 'Keywords' sheets are not included.

The workbook lists responsibilities as DPH summarizes them; the statute or regulation citation controls. A footnote in the workbook says OLRH has received comments that the standards marked * are outdated.

The workbook has no status, due dates, or scoring: those are for each department to record. The next version of the Performance Standards is expected to include the Foundational Public Health Services framework (DPH's FPHS page).
State program contact phone numbers and email addresses are not copied; the program names are kept.

workforce_notes: **Board members performing inspections must meet the requirements under "Inspector/Environmental Health Specialist"

*Management positions should meet the requirements as set forth in this document for the position. However, a request may be submitted by the board of health to waive the Registered Sanitarian (RS) requirement if: 1) the Health Department has a management position and a separate full-time Environmental Health Director and; 2) the Environmental Health Director has an RS, oversees the inspectors, and reports directly to the management position.
• All personnel should have at least ICS 100/NIMS 700 within 1 year of hire. Those who might have a leadership role should have ICS 200 and above.
• Boards of health may have stricter requirements, but they must meet these requirements.

• Boards of health with current staff who have worked for local or state public health for at least 7 years, but who do not meet these requirements, may request a waiver except for inspectional trainings.

• Membership in professional organizations is deemed as critical for professional development, for leadership and mentoring opportunities, and for opportunities for sharing best practices. This is recommended, but not required.
